title: SAFF: Scalable Acceleration of GNN-based Machine Learning Force Fields using Tensor-Aware Hardware for Molecular Simulation
problem: GNN-based machine learning force fields for molecular dynamics have high tensor product computational workload. High-dimensional tensors cause memory bottlenecks limiting GPU resource utilization. Current performance inadequate for practical semiconductor process simulations.
motivation: Accelerate molecular dynamics simulations to enable practical use in semiconductor process simulation.
method: The approach fuses multiple tensor mathematical operations into single combined steps, keeping intermediate data in the GPU's fast on-chip memory rather than moving it back to slower main memory—this solves the memory bottleneck that was limiting performance. It also restructures the computation to eliminate redundant operations. A specialized hardware architecture is then designed specifically to perform the tensor products that graph neural networks use to calculate molecular forces.
key_novelty: Custom hardware architecture designed specifically for the tensor operations in graph neural network-based molecular force calculations.
contributions: Tensor-based function fusion increasing data continuity and on-chip reuse
Dedicated tensor product hardware architecture for GNN-based MLFF
Computation flow restructuring eliminating redundant operations
limitations: Specialized to GNN-based force fields; generalization to other tensor-heavy workloads unclear.
